title: Etale-local infinitesimal solutions imply smoothness
statement: Let $f:V\to W$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Suppose that for every first order thickening $i:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ of affine schemes (a closed immersion defined by an ideal $\mathcal I$ with $\mathcal I^2=0$) [def-sbc-first-order-thickening] and scheme maps $a_0:T_0\to V$, $b:T\to W$ with $fa_0=bi$, there is a jointly surjective family of etale maps $v_j:T_j\to T$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] and maps $a_j:T_j\to V$ with $fa_j=bv_j$ and $a_j|_{T_0\times_TT_j}=a_0\operatorname{pr}_{T_0}$, where the product is the scheme fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $f$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

source.place: Tag 04AM (lemma-smooth-formally-smooth), proof: sheaf of lifts and its torsor under the derivation module (Tags 061A lemma-sheaf, 061C lemma-action-sheaf), restricted to schemes; vanishing of H^1 of a quasi-coherent module on an affine etale site, etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03P2 (theorem-zariski-fpqc-quasi-coherent); conclusion via more-morphisms.tex Tag 02H6 (lemma-smooth-formally-smooth).

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary affine first-order thickening $i:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ and maps $a_0,b$ satisfying $fa_0=bi$. Apply [lem-sfb-etale-local-lift-torsor-quasi-coherent] to this square. It gives the quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_T$-module $\mathcal H$, the etale sheaf $\mathcal L$ of compatible lifts, and the simply transitive $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{et}}$-action wherever a section exists.

source.place: Tag 04AM, lemma-smooth-formally-smooth, sheaf-of-lifts torsor argument; Tags 061A, 061C, 061D for the lift sheaf and its action, restricted to schemes.

proof.text: For each member $v_j:T_j\to T$ of the jointly surjective etale family in the hypothesis, the given $a_j$ is a section of $\mathcal L(T_j)$, since its two compatibility identities are exactly the defining identities of $\mathcal L$. Translation by $a_j$ identifies the restriction of $\mathcal L$ to $T_j$ with that of $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{et}}$: the bijections from Step 1 hold after every further restriction. Thus $\mathcal L$ is an $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{et}}$-torsor in the general abelian-sheaf sense of [def-sc-gm-torsor].

source.place: Tag 04AM, lemma-smooth-formally-smooth, sheaf-of-lifts torsor argument; Tags 061A, 061C, 061D for the lift sheaf and its action, restricted to schemes.

proof.text: Since $T$ is affine and $\mathcal H$ is quasi-coherent, [lem-sc-etale-affine-qcoherent] with $q=1$ gives $H^1(T_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal H_{\mathrm{et}})=0$. This applies to the module on $T$, not to a module on $T_0$ without a comparison.

The torsor classification [lem-sc-torsor-h1] sends the trivial torsor to zero and is bijective. Step 3 therefore forces the torsor $\mathcal L$ from Step 2 to be isomorphic to the trivial torsor $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{et}}$. The inverse image of its zero global section is an element of $\mathcal L(T)$; by the defining section condition this is a map $a:T\to V$ with $fa=b$ and $ai=a_0$.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1, zero class and trivial torsor.

proof.text: The preceding construction works for every affine first-order thickening and every compatible pair $a_0,b$. These are precisely the quantified lifting problems in [def-sbc-formally-smooth], so $f$ is formally smooth.
Combine formal smoothness from Step 5 with the original locally finite presentation hypothesis. By [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], these two properties say that $f$ is smooth.
